summary: A single-author, book-length practitioner guide (v1.4, ~1.7M characters, 31 chapters) that runs from transformer internals, RL alignment (PPO/DPO/GRPO) and inference systems through RAG, agent memory, harness design, loop and graph engineering, MCP, skills, A2A, multi-agent systems, frameworks, evaluation and regulation. Its running example is a LangGraph/Ollama multi-agent glucose-monitoring assistant (the 'Guardian Angel System'), with notebooks. It reports no new experiments.

claims.claim: Building great agentic systems requires understanding every layer of the pipeline, not just one.
claims.evidence: Thesis stated in abstract/Preface; argued by exposition, not evaluated.

claims.claim: A poorly designed harness can nullify the capabilities of even the most powerful LLM.
claims.evidence: Chapter 18 introduction asserts this; supported only by citations to secondary literature, no measurement in the document.

claims.claim: The guide is an accurate reference to primary literature.
claims.evidence: Disclaimer states LLMs were used as a research and drafting aid and content was verified 'on a best-effort basis'; no external review. Accuracy of individual claims not checked in this review beyond chapter structure.

patterns.note: Chapter 24 on Agent Skills and procedural memory (§17.2.4).
Chapters 18-20 harness orchestration, loop vs graph engineering.
Chapter 12 agentic training and harness distillation (§12.6).

methodology.models: Running example uses llama3.2 via Ollama.

standards.peer_review: None; arXiv comment 'version 1.4'; v3 on arXiv, living document.

biases.detail: Author discloses LLM drafting assistance with best-effort verification; high risk of unverified or hallucinated details in a 1.7M-character text.
Promotional framing ('the reference I wish I had', 'full stack').
Survey/textbook with no systematic literature-selection protocol and no new evidence.

coi.affiliations: Single author Haggai Roitman; no affiliation stated (disclaimer disclaims employer views). The regex 'GitHub' vendor hit is a false positive from repository URLs.
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: None evaluated; frameworks (LangGraph, AutoGen, OpenAI Agents SDK, etc.) described.

verdict_reason: An unreviewed, LLM-assisted textbook with no empirical contribution and no systematic review method. It can serve as a background glossary, but none of its claims should be weighted as evidence in the KB.
applicability: Usable only as orientation reading for team members new to agent harness vocabulary (harness, loop engineering, MCP, skills, memory). It gives no evidence for harness decisions for a Java multi-repo work team: there is no Java, no multi-repo coordination, no spec-driven development, and no mixed-host material. The medical running example (glucose monitoring) is clinical decision support, not domain data.
